name: Background Sync
plain: Retries a request later when the connection returns, after the tab closes.
meaning: Lets a site send queued data (a message, a form, a like) once the device is back online even if the person has left. Quiet and automatic, so no prompt is shown.

access.prompt_ui: No prompt; the Permissions API reports background-sync as always granted.
access.persistence: Tied to the service worker registration
access.revocation: Unregister the service worker or clear site data
steps: Register a sync tag from the page
Browser fires sync in the service worker when online
On failure the browser retries with backoff, lastChance on the final try

fields.name: retries
fields.range: 3 attempts with exponential backoff in Chrome

limits.headline: Can retry sending queued data after you close the tab, once you are back online
limits.user_action: You tap Send or Save while offline, then leave the page
can: Send a saved message, form or like later when your device is online again
Finish quietly in the background without a pop up
Retry a few times if sending fails
cannot: Do anything open ended; it only sends items the page already queued
Keep trying forever, since the browser stops it after a few tries
Show you any prompt or notice that it ran
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet only. Firefox, Safari and iPhone browsers do not support it.

story.what_it_is: A site can retry a failed action later, once your connection returns, even after you close the tab.

marketing.name: Background Synchronization API
marketing.pitch: Defer actions until the user has a stable connection, so work is sent even if the tab closes.

story.for_you: You send a message or form while offline. The site says it will send later. When your phone gets signal, it goes out without reopening the page.
story.for_makers: Makers use it so users never lose a post, order or edit because of a bad connection. It builds trust and cuts support issues. It only runs in Chromium browsers.

use_cases.example: You post in a web chat on a subway. The post is queued, and sends itself after you leave the tunnel and close the browser.
A web note app saves your note locally, and sends it to the cloud when the signal returns.
A web store queues an order placed in a weak signal area, and completes it later.
A browser game sends your final score or save data later, so a lost signal does not erase progress.
A web design tool uploads your latest edits in the background when the network is back.
A web health log syncs your entries to the clinic when the connection returns.
A web app sends queued usage events later, so measurement does not drop when the user is offline.

technical_bounds: Only when the browser process runs and the device is online
